packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.eventbus
packages.summary: A lightweight, thread-safe publish-subscribe event system for loosely coupled components.

types.name: EventBus
types.javadoc_summary: A publish-subscribe event bus that simplifies communication between components.

methods.name: getDefault
methods.signature: @SuppressFBWarnings("MS_EXPOSE_REP") public static EventBus getDefault()
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the default `EventBus` instance.
methods.returns: the default `EventBus` instance
contract: On a standard JVM its worker threads are daemon threads: they never keep the JVM alive, and deliveries still queued when the JVM exits may be abandoned.

A shutdown hook, installed when the first default worker is created, gives them up to 120 seconds to drain; no hook is installed if that happens while the JVM is already shutting down or while a security manager denies `RuntimePermission("shutdownHooks")`.

When this library is shared by several applications (a container-level library, for example), give each application's bus its own executor through #create(String, Executor) and shut that executor down when the application stops.

Conversely, a JVM shutdown hook keeps this library's own class loader reachable until exit once the default executor has created a worker or a caller-supplied executor service has been registered; an application that bundles this library and must be unloadable should deliver only synchronously or, better, use a copy of this library loaded by a shared class loader.
examples:
EventBus eventBus = EventBus.getDefault();
 eventBus.post("Hello World");

methods.signature: public static EventBus create(final String identifier, final Executor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: identifier
params.javadoc: a label for this `EventBus`, returned by #identifier(); it need not be unique and may be `null`

params.name: executor
params.javadoc: the executor to use for asynchronous event delivery; must not be `null`

throws.condition: if `executor` is `null`.

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates a new `EventBus` instance with the specified identifier and executor.
methods.returns: a new `EventBus` instance with the given identifier and executor
contract: The executor is used for asynchronous event delivery when ThreadMode#THREAD_POOL_EXECUTOR is specified.
If the supplied executor is an ExecutorService other than the shared default executor or ForkJoinPool#commonPool(), it is registered, by identity, with a single process-wide JVM shutdown hook.

That can happen to a decorator over a pool, such as `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()`, while the pool behind it is still running queued deliveries; keep a reference to such an executor service, or shut it down yourself, when those deliveries must complete at exit.
examples:
ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4);
 EventBus eventBus = EventBus.create("myEventBus", executor);

params.javadoc: the event ID override; must be non-empty for lambda-based subscribers; `null` or empty preserves each handler's annotation-level event ID (or no ID if none is declared)

params.javadoc: the thread mode override for event delivery, or `null` to use the thread mode declared in each subscriber method's Subscribe annotation

if a `@Subscribe` method of the subscriber's class or a superclass is `static` (whatever its visibility), or if a `public` instance `@Subscribe` method of the class or any supertype does not declare exactly one parameter, or (java.lang.reflect.InaccessibleObjectException) if a handler method cannot be made accessible, for example one in a non-public class whose package is in a named module not opened to this library

methods.javadoc_summary: Registers a subscriber with both event ID and thread mode specifications.
methods.returns: this `EventBus` instance for method chaining
contract: If the subscriber has sticky event handling enabled, it will immediately receive any matching sticky events; delivery of those sticky events respects each handler's effective ThreadMode (the registration override if given, otherwise the annotation's), so a `THREAD_POOL_EXECUTOR` sticky delivery is handed to this bus's executor: with the default executor it runs on a background thread, but a caller-supplied direct executor (such as `Runnable::run`) runs it on the registering thread before `register` returns.
A sticky event removed while this call is replaying is skipped if its turn has not yet come, but one already being replayed is still delivered.
Likewise, the replay stops once the subscriber is unregistered or registered again (the new registration replays for itself), even when its own handler does so.
examples: eventBus.register(mySubscriber, "userEvents", ThreadMode.THREAD_POOL_EXECUTOR);

methods.name: post
methods.signature: public EventBus post(final String eventId, final Object event) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: eventId
params.javadoc: the event ID for filtering subscribers, or `null` (or empty) to deliver to subscribers without a specific event ID

params.name: event
params.javadoc: the event to post

throws.condition: if `event` is `null`.

methods.javadoc_summary: Posts an event with an optional event ID.
methods.returns: this `EventBus` instance for method chaining
contract: When `eventId` is non-`null` and non-empty, the event is delivered only to handlers whose effective event ID equals it: handlers of subscribers registered with that event ID, and handlers whose Subscribe#eventId() specifies it when their subscriber was registered without an event ID (a registration-time event ID replaces the annotation's).
The handler must also accept the event's runtime type (exactly, for a `strictEventType` handler).
When `eventId` is `null` or empty, the event is delivered to all subscribers that have no event ID filter (equivalent to calling #post(Object)).
examples:
eventBus.post("userEvents", new UserLoginEvent(userId));
 // Only subscribers associated with "userEvents" will receive this

types.name: Subscribe
types.javadoc_summary: Marks a method as an event subscriber in the EventBus system.

methods.name: threadMode
methods.signature: ThreadMode threadMode() default ThreadMode.DEFAULT
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the thread mode for event delivery.
methods.returns: the thread mode for event delivery

methods.name: strictEventType
methods.signature: boolean strictEventType() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Controls whether the subscriber accepts only exact event type matches or includes subtypes.
methods.returns: `true` to accept only exact type matches, `false` to accept subtypes
contract: When set to `true`, only events of the exact parameter type will be delivered.
When `false` (default), events of the parameter type and all its subtypes will be delivered.

methods.name: sticky
methods.signature: boolean sticky() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Indicates whether this subscriber should receive previously posted sticky events upon registration.
methods.returns: `true` to receive sticky events upon registration
contract: When `true`, every retained sticky event matching this subscriber's type and effective event ID is dispatched to this subscriber during registration, in its thread mode.
Replayed events pass through the same #intervalMillis() and #deduplicate() filters as posted events, so when either is enabled some matching retained events may be suppressed.
When several retained sticky events match, the order in which they are replayed is unspecified.

methods.name: eventId
methods.signature: String eventId() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies an event ID to filter incoming events.
methods.returns: the event ID to filter on, or an empty string to match events posted without an event ID
contract: If empty (default) and no registration-level event ID is supplied, the subscriber receives only events posted without an event ID, matched by type.

methods.name: intervalMillis
methods.signature: long intervalMillis() default 0
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the minimum time interval (in milliseconds) between accepted delivery attempts.
methods.returns: the minimum interval between accepted attempts in milliseconds; any value `<= 0` disables throttling
contract: Accepted callbacks may overlap if a callback runs longer than the interval; a failed callback still counts as an attempt, while a submission for which `Executor.execute` throws (for example a `RejectedExecutionException` under the default `AbortPolicy`) does not, because it was never delivered - unless its task had already begun the callback by the time the bus handled that failure.
Any value `<= 0` is likewise treated as "no throttling": the `EventBus` delivery guard only throttles when the interval is strictly positive, so a negative interval has the same effect as `0`.

methods.name: deduplicate
methods.signature: boolean deduplicate() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Controls whether duplicate consecutive events should be ignored.
methods.returns: `true` to ignore duplicate consecutive events
contract: When `true`, an event equal to the event of this subscriber's most recently accepted delivery attempt is ignored.
If the posted event's `equals()` throws, that event is not delivered to this handler and the previous event is kept, so later events are still compared against it.

params.name: event

methods.javadoc_summary: Called when a matching event is posted to the EventBus; see the class description for how `E` is matched (a lambda typed as `Subscriber<E>` itself receives every event posted with its event ID, whatever its type).
